$description: Trellis token source, in the W3C Design Tokens format. One seed for every platform: lengths are in cells or in points, never in rem or px. A point is one CSS pixel at the reader's default text size, one pt on iOS, one dp on Android. tools/build-tokens.js writes the generated tokens of core.css from this file, and does the rem conversion for the web. Formulas (the fit, the ratio, the gutter) are not values and are not here: see math.js.

cell.$description: The cell, the measure of space. Its target grows in a straight line from the narrow screen to the wide one, then holds, and it follows the reader's text size.

target-narrow.$description: The cell on a narrow screen.

target-wide.$description: The cell on a wide screen.

screen-narrow.$description: Up to this width the cell is target-narrow.

screen-wide.$description: From this width the cell is target-wide.

text-scale-max.$description: The cap on the cell: it follows the reader's text size up to this many times the default, and no further. Above it only type grows, and layouts reflow.

frame.$description: The page's outer box, in cells.

space.$description: The octaves: the cell halved and doubled. Between blocks, space is whole cells; halves and quarters live inside things.

q.$description: A quarter cell, rounded to a whole pixel and never less than a line.

size.$description: Named sizes, each an octave or an octave plus a line.

base.$description: One cell plus a line each side.

hit-min.$description: The least hit area on a coarse pointer, whatever a control draws. A platform layer turns this: 44 on iOS, 48 on Android.

control-type.$description: Control labels: fixed sizes, not fluid. The only font sizes outside the type roles.

radius.$description: Corners are octaves too. A nested corner is the outer corner less the padding.

layer.$description: One scale for everything that stacks.

type.$description: The ratio's neutral defaults. Two anchors, H1 and body, each with a size in a narrow space and a wide one; headings step down from H1 by one ratio and paragraphs step out from body by another, and both ratios open with the space. A product layer turns all of these.

color.$description: A relational palette: a few seeds, and every role derived from one. A product sets the seeds (and may turn the lift, the flip and the gradient settings); it never sets a role. Seeds are OKLCH, each in its light-theme form. math.js derives every role from these in arithmetic; core.css does it with relative colors.

seed.$description: One color each. The neutral seed gives the neutral roles their hue and chroma (its lightness is not used). Every other seed is a hue: the accent, the five kinds (what sort of thing this is; shape and color both follow kind; topic is also the default tag) and the three statuses.

accent.$description: The primary action, and the focus ring.

lift.$description: How much lighter a hue is in the dark theme, in OKLCH lightness.

ink-flip.$description: Ink on a fill: white on a fill darker than this lightness, a dark ink of the fill's own hue on a lighter one.

neutral.$description: Neutral roles: the neutral seed's hue and chroma at a lightness for each theme.

gradient.$description: A gradient is an interpolation space and its stops, from roles; the author adds a direction or a shape.

turn.$description: How far the accent gradient turns its hue, in degrees.
